title: DF-LoGiT: Data-Free Logic-Gated Backdoor Attacks in Vision Transformers
claim: Our attack hides a trigger-gated signal across model stages, so it is carried through the network untouched and injected only when the gate fires.
layout: 4 stage panels, left-to-right, nested blocks, red signal path, color legend below
description: A wide four-stage diagram flows left to right. On the far left, an input image with small patch triggers feeds a patch-embedding bar. Stage 1 and Stage 2 share one grey panel containing ViT Block 0. It shows multi-head attention with edited heads writing per-trigger bits into a CLS token, then an MLP whose neuron acts as an m-of-n gate with GELU units. Stage 3 shows blocks 1–10 as a residual highway where the signal passes through unchanged. Stage 4 shows block 11 with a conditional MLP injection, then a classifier head that outputs the target label (goldfish) instead of the benign label (cat). Blue marks benign pre-trained components. Red marks triggers, edited parameters and backdoor signals, and a red path traces the signal across all stages. A legend sits at the bottom.
caption: Overview of logic-gated, data-free backdoor attacks in Vision Transformers via m-of-n Boolean triggers.
abstract: The widespread adoption of Vision Transformers (ViTs) elevates supply-chain risk on third-party model hubs, where an adversary can implant backdoors into released checkpoints. Existing ViT backdoor attacks largely rely on poisoned-data training, while prior data-free attempts typically require synthetic-data fine-tuning or extra model components. This paper introduces Data-Free Logic-Gated Backdoor Attacks (DF-LoGiT), a truly data-free backdoor attack on ViTs via direct weight editing. DF-LoGiT exploits ViT's native multi-head architecture to realize a logic-gated compositional trigger, enabling a stealthy and effective backdoor. We validate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and extensive experiments, showing that DF-LoGiT achieves near-100% attack success with negligible degradation in benign accuracy and remains robust against representative classical and ViT-specific defenses.
